clue.text: Food here for a friar to give away

parts.note: Friar Tuck is the jovial friar of the Robin Hood legends
to shop someone is slang for betraying them to the police

explanation.surface: A remark about food being handed out by a charitable friar.
explanation.walkthrough: A tuck shop is a school snack shop in Britain; 'tuck' is British school slang for sweets and cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A school snack kiosk is where pupils buy their sweets and buns, so it is where food is found.

clue.text: Calm as the mind 4 bid farewell

definitions.meaning: in Shakespeare's play, the Moor of 4-down cries 'Farewell the ... mind! farewell content!'

explanation.walkthrough: The 4 refers to the answer at 4-down, the Moor of Venice, whose famous farewell speech supplies the quotation.
explanation.definitionFit: Calm and the quoted adjective both describe a peaceful, serene state; the second sense is a direct quotation from Shakespeare.

clue.text: Broadcast extremely prophetic parable of the fruit-tree

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
extremely points to the outermost letters of the word prophetic

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A prophetic parable about a fruit tree being broadcast to listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes P and C from 'prophetic'; 'Broadcast' scatters PC with PARABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: This small sour-fruited tree is a wild kind of apple tree, so it is a fruit-tree.

clue.text: Butterfly in evidence one day a year

parts.note: Sat is the short form of Saturday, one day of the week
yr is the standard abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A butterfly that shows itself on just one day each year.
explanation.definitionFit: The satyrs are a family of brown butterflies with eyespots on their wings, so the word names a butterfly.

clue.text: Look up and down when crossing the Moor

indicators.note: crossing means one piece spans across and around another
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look
taken as written
lo again means look, here read downwards in normal order

explanation.surface: Advice to glance about warily when crossing a stretch of moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up and down' gives LO twice: once reversed (up) as OL, which straddles THE, then once read normally (down). 'Moor' is not the heath but Shakespeare's Moor of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic hero is the Moor of Venice, so the capitalised word names him.

clue.text: Posh fur ready to wear

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in the old U and non-U distinction
sable is the fur of a small marten

explanation.surface: An upper-class fur coat that is ready to put on.
explanation.walkthrough: U for upper-class comes from 1950s British talk of 'U and non-U' speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit to be put on or employed for its purpose is fit for use.

clue.text: Ass in south with a lot of money procures explosive device

parts.note: moke is British slang for a donkey
a bomb is British slang for a large sum of money

explanation.surface: A donkey in the south with plenty of cash buys a dangerous gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: MOKE (British slang for donkey) goes in after S; 'cost a bomb' is British for being very expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister that releases dense smoke when set off is a kind of explosive device.

clue.text: Agent runs off, leaving one bankrupt

indicators.note: runs off means the letter for runs is taken away

parts.note: a broker is an agent who buys and sells for others
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An agent flees, leaving someone ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes the R (runs, from cricket scoring) from BROKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being penniless and unable to pay debts is the slang sense of the word, a synonym for insolvent.

clue.text: Enrol in new Light Infantry mustered in east of France

indicators.note: mustered in says the new troops are gathered inside the word for east

parts.note: est is French for east
LI is the military abbreviation for Light Infantry

explanation.surface: New recruits join the Light Infantry and assemble in eastern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mustered in' is the container signal: the troops gather inside the French word for east, which 'of France' flags as foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up, especially for military service, is to register or join, the same as to enrol.

clue.text: Braved rioting, for example, unwisely

indicators.note: rioting suggests the letters running wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly defied a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rioting' rearranges BRAVED. The definition is by example: 'unwisely' is a word of that grammatical class.
explanation.definitionFit: The word unwisely modifies a verb, making it an instance of that part of speech.

clue.text: Look forward to a humorist accepting an article

indicators.note: accepting means the comedian's word takes another letter inside it

parts.note: a wit is a humorous person
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Anticipating a comedian who takes on a written piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts A (an article) inside WIT; the first A stands as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: To expect or wait for something coming is to anticipate it.

clue.text: Henry Ford rejected viscous fuel for this vessel

parts.note: Hy is a short form of the name Henry

indicators.note: rejected means the word is turned back, read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
oil is a thick, viscous fuel

explanation.surface: Henry Ford turns down a thick fuel for a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' is the reversal signal. The surface evokes the carmaker, but Henry and Ford are separate pieces; Hy is a pet form of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat with underwater wings that lift its hull clear of the water is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: A boring device in that Parisian card-game

indicators.note: in places the boring tool inside the French word

parts.note: que is French for that
a drill is a tool for boring holes

explanation.surface: A drilling tool features in a Parisian card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; 'that Parisian' asks for the French word. The card game, popular in the 1700s, shares its name with the square dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides the dance, this word names an old card game for four players, a forerunner of whist.

clue.text: Vessels removing source of silt from channels

indicators.note: removing means a letter is taken out of the word for channels

parts.note: sewers are channels carrying waste water

indicators.note: source of points to the first letter of silt

explanation.surface: Silt being cleared from waterways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' gives S, the first letter of 'silt'; 'removing' takes it off SEWERS.
explanation.definitionFit: These are large jugs or pitchers for water, which are containers, a sense of vessels.

clue.text: Concerning one member leading the relief work

indicators.note: leading says the first two pieces come before the word for concerning

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP stands for Member of Parliament
as to means concerning or regarding

explanation.surface: A remark about a politician heading a relief effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading' puts I and MP in front of AS TO. 'Relief work' is not aid but raised painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint laid on thickly so that it stands out from the canvas gives a raised, sculpted effect.

clue.text: Guardsman here making second appearance on TV

parts.note: an entry is an appearance, as of an actor on stage
the box is British slang for television

explanation.surface: A soldier showing up again on television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The box' is everyday British slang for the television.
explanation.definitionFit: The small hut a sentinel stands in is where the guardsman is stationed.

clue.text: Mount for a fellow sergeant, perhaps?

parts.note: bro is short for brother, a fellow or mate
a sergeant is an example of an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A horse provided for a soldier's comrade, a sergeant.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbroken horse of the American West is something one rides, which is a mount.

clue.text: Island boat's first carpenter, for instance

indicators.note: first says the boat's word is placed before the island

parts.note: craft is a boat; with the possessive it gives craft's
Man is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: An island boat's first carpenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' puts CRAFT'S ahead of MAN, the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is a skilled worker with his hands, so an example of an artisan.

clue.text: Many were prone increasingly to display a sword

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
lay is the past tense of lie, so were lying prone
more indicates something growing in degree

explanation.surface: Many people lay down more and more to show off a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: C for 'many' is a crossword convention from the Roman numeral 100.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish two-handed broadsword is the weapon named here.

clue.text: A note from Caruso, say

indicators.note: say signals a word that sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: Enrico Caruso was a famous operatic tenor

explanation.surface: A musical note sung by the great opera singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is a banknote, not music: a tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A ten-pound banknote is one piece of paper money, which is a note in British usage.

clue.text: Hero's terrific contribution to the roll of names

indicators.note: contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hero makes a great contribution to a list of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of people's names, as for a duty rota, is a register or roll.

clue.text: Male dog given this by dockers?

definitions.text: Male dog given this by dockers?

parts.words: Male dog given this by dockers?
parts.note: dockers suggests harbour workers, but here means people who cut short an animal's tail

explanation.definitionFit: A docked tail is cut short, so a dog with its tail docked is left with a stubby one.

clue.text: Clump of ferns blown by the wind in the mountain

indicators.note: in places the wind-driven word inside the mountain

parts.note: ben is a Scottish word for a mountain
to rack is to be driven along before the wind, like clouds

explanation.surface: Ferns tossed by the wind on a mountainside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. 'Blown by the wind' looks like part of the definition but supplies the old verb for clouds scudding before a gale.
explanation.definitionFit: A large coarse fern growing in dense stands on hillsides forms a mass of ferns.

clue.text: VIP's wife in second-rate musical set-up

definitions.note: the 's reads as is, a link joining the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: B is a second-class grade

indicators.note: in places the wife inside the reversed show
in a down clue, set-up means the word is lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: Gigi is a Lerner and Loewe musical

explanation.surface: A celebrity's wife appears in a poor musical production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' turns GIGI round to IGIG; 'in' puts W inside it after B. 'Musical set-up' looks like a band, but it is the show reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An important, influential person is slangily called this, a synonym for VIP.

clue.text: Suffer from cold in popular old city

indicators.note: in places the cold letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Someone suffering from a cold in a popular ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal, putting the cold letter between the two other pieces; Ur is the Biblical city of Abraham.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something unpleasant on oneself, such as a cost or a penalty, is to sustain it.

clue.text: Navigation of vessel by a learner

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel
L is for learner, from the L-plates on British learner cars

explanation.surface: Steering of a boat by a novice.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a 'navigation' is an old name for an artificial waterway; L comes from learner-driver L-plates.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage an artificial waterway built for boats is called a navigation.

clue.text: Like packets moving safely on rollers

definitions.text: Like packets moving safely on rollers

parts.words: Like packets moving safely on rollers
parts.note: packets are packet boats and rollers are big waves, so this describes ships fit to sail

explanation.definitionFit: A ship that can safely put to sea in heavy waves is in good condition for voyages.

clue.text: Extravagant note unacceptable to the Head

indicators.note: to the head means the word for unacceptable goes to the top of this down entry

parts.note: out means not allowed or unacceptable
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A lavish message the headteacher will not accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the Head' moves OUT to the top, above RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something bizarre or beyond the bounds of convention is outlandish or over the top.

clue.text: Come to blows fearlessly with this for protection?

definitions.text: Come to blows fearlessly with this for protection?

parts.words: Come to blows fearlessly with this for protection?
parts.note: come to blows suggests fighting, but here means the gale arriving, which a screen of trees lets you face without fear

explanation.definitionFit: A hedge or fence that shelters against gusts gives protection when gales blow.

clue.text: Rate of activity encountered on return to river

indicators.note: on return means the word is turned back, read right to left

parts.note: met means encountered
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: How busy things were, met on the way back to the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' is the reversal signal; the Po flows across northern Italy into the Adriatic.
explanation.definitionFit: The pace or speed at which something happens is its rhythm or speed.

clue.text: A brilliant company for the festival, with two unknowns

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
x and y are the usual unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A dazzling troupe arriving for the festival, with two strangers.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a star system, the word means a glittering assembly of famous people.

clue.text: Censors, we hear, work in pairs

definitions.text: Censors, we hear, work in pairs

parts.words: Censors, we hear, work in pairs
parts.note: censors sounds like sensors, and an insect's feelers are sensors that come two at a time

explanation.definitionFit: An insect's feelers are sensory organs and always grow as a matched couple on its head.
